item.title: Modern Perl Tips
item.description:
Dave wrote: "Talking to Perl programmers, I’ve noticed how easy it is to miss new additions to the language. We learn Perl, get comfortable with it, and get on with writing code. Meanwhile, Perl keeps moving
Modern Perl Tips is a chance to catch up a little at a time. Each tip takes a useful feature you might not have come across, shows how it helps with an everyday problem, and points you towards the documentation. You might discover a clearer way to write something you’ve been doing for years."
item.author: dave_cross

item.title: Adventures in Real-Time MIDI
item.description: Gene writes: "Since discovering Perl real-time MIDI and writing about creating async drums with it, I’ve dug deeper into what’s possible. I have a few music and MIDI modules on CPAN and like to put them to use in real time, now that I have been enlightened by zen master John Barrett. Ha :D"
item.author: gene_boggs

item.title: URI::PackageURL 2.26 released: PURL and VERS for Perl
item.description: URI-PackageURL implements two specifications that are becoming central to software supply-chain security: PURL (Package URL, a uniform way to identify a software package across ecosystems ) and VERS ((Version Range, a universal notation for version ranges)

item.title: HAMT: persistent maps, sets and vectors for Perl
item.description: HAMT is a new CPAN distribution that gives Perl three persistent containers: HAMT::Map, HAMT::Set and HAMT::Vector. "Persistent" here means an update never changes the container you call it on. It returns a new one, and the old one stays exactly as it was.
item.author: robert_acock

item.title: Time::Keeper: Time goes by so slowly
item.description: Time::Keeper is a new CPAN distribution for dates and times. A value is an instant and the zone it is read in, and that is the whole of it: no state to mutate, no locale object, no copy of the zone rules. It covers the ground Time::Piece and DateTime cover between them, and a method that would change a value hands back a new one and leaves the old one as it was.
item.author: robert_acock
